answer: A beacon picks one of three hash-prefix batches (walnut, wharf, quartz) after each close, and 15 % of it, about 5 % of settled rows, is re-judged by a fresh four-seat panel drawn from established accounts outside the original jury. A grader disagreeing with the shadow median on over 30 % of its audited rows loses its seats for 12 epochs. A ring holding seat share s controls both panels with probability s^8 (s = 0.3: 0.007 %). Weakness: five graders holding 81 % of seats, as in E33, make the pool too narrow, and the cheapest bypass is joining the established set.
